title: Canva authorization code in the redirect URL code query parameter
summary: An authorization code delivered to the app's redirect URL as the code query parameter, beside state, and exchanged with the code_verifier and client authentication.
rationale: Claim code-redirect-query-parameter names the carrier (a required code query parameter of a browser redirect, by design) and claim code-exchange-inputs records that the exchange needs the code, the code_verifier and client authentication together, and cannot be called from a browser client. Canva states confidentiality only for the code_verifier and the client secret (claim code-verifier-role-and-confidentiality); whether the code alone is a credential is a modelling decision the sources do not make (open question code-confidentiality-unstated). Its lifetime and single use are not stated: the only single-use rule is for refresh tokens (claim single-use-stated-for-refresh-token-only, open question code-lifetime-and-single-use-unstated). No format is stated (code-format-and-example-unstated). A must-flag would rest on a confidentiality statement Canva does not make; the code_challenge's confidentiality is unstated too, so no derived-value control is written. Contract claims cited: authorization-code/code-redirect-query-parameter, authorization-code/code-exchange-inputs, authorization-code/single-use-stated-for-refresh-token-only.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Settled by: a Canva statement of the code's lifetime and single use or of its confidentiality.
